name: Hindustan Construction Company Ltd
title: Hindustan Construction Company Ltd - 500185 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Order book of ₹12,901 crore is stalled, with management guiding to doubling it by FY-end on pending hydro bids; standalone EBITDA margin fell to 12.2% from 16.1%, and no capacity or supply-side signals were given.

summary.headline: HCC Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin fell to 12.2% from 16.1% while order book stands at ₹12,901 crore, with management targeting a near doubling by year-end.
summary.overview: Standalone turnover was ₹895.8 crore (presentation) or ₹923 crore (CFO), against ₹975 crore a year earlier, with standalone net profit of ₹36.8 crore roughly flat YoY. Consolidated revenue was ₹896.8 crore with profit of ₹22.6 crore, and the CFO cited consolidated EBITDA of ₹102 crore. Management said orders of ₹524 crore were secured in the half, and it is awaiting results on bids worth over ₹34,800 crore under evaluation. Debt prepayment of ₹100 crore was made in Q2, with a further ₹108 crore targeted by December 2026. The call was dominated by questions on the order book, margin decline and consolidated profit.

segments.name: Transportation (surface transport, bridges, underground metro)
segments.commentary: Largest share of the ₹12,901 crore order book. Indore Metro TBM tunnelling (12 km, seven underground stations) has started with both machines running; Mumbai Coastal Road Package 2 won an ENR Global Best Project award for bridges and tunnels.

segments.name: Hydropower
segments.commentary: Bhivpuri PSP (1,000 MW, Tata Power) powerhouse and main access tunnel complete. Vishnugad Pipalkoti about 80% complete with 830 m of HRT TBM tunnelling left. Management said recent bidding has been weighted to hydro, where client clearances are delaying awards.

segments.name: Nuclear, water and other
segments.commentary: FRFCF facility about 87% complete. Parwan Dam completed with reservoir filling test done; ancillary works due over the next three to four months. Salal Dam hydromechanical rectification work has begun. Hindalco pot shell and superstructure production is ongoing.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the order book to roughly double by year-end (the CEO's and COO's timeline, later described as the financial year), supported by bids of over ₹34,800 crore under evaluation.
Long-term standalone EBITDA margin guided at 13-14% on a YoY basis; management said quarterly margins will not match this range.
Consolidated and standalone numbers expected to align on revenue and profitability within a couple of quarters, as subsidiary interest accruals stop.
Debt liability of about ₹350 crore due in March 2027 after the Q2 prepayment; management aims to be debt-free within the next couple of years.
Award money from a Supreme Court matter expected to be released in Q3 FY27.
Patna Metro mobilisation (diaphragm wall equipment, machine procurement) under way; Agardanda Creek Bridge superstructure erection to start in about one month.

financial_highlights.change: Versus ₹975 crore in Q2 FY26 per CFO; the two figures are not reconciled in the call

financial_highlights.value: ₹22.6 crore (presentation); profit after tax almost ₹23 crore (CFO)
financial_highlights.change: Declined per analyst; attributed to interest accruals on loans to insignificant subsidiaries

financial_highlights.value: ₹2,010 crore of bids, HCC share ₹1,557 crore

qa_highlights.question: Why has standalone EBITDA margin fallen to about 12% from 16% a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said construction is seasonal and quarterly margin depends on the mix of high- and low-margin projects; long-term standalone EBITDA margin guided at 13-14% YoY, which management hopes to reach by year-end, though not every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is top-line flat while net profit grows, and why did consolidated profit decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said standalone drives numbers; consolidated decline reflects accounting interest accruals on loans to insignificant subsidiaries, not material operating losses. Order book stagnation was cited for weak growth.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the subsidiary-related expense drag on consolidated P&L last, and will standalone and consolidated align?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the impact should last a couple of quarters as interest accruals stop, and confirmed standalone and consolidated should match on revenue and profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Why are L1 positions not converting into orders, and what is the bid success ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: COO said hydro orders need client clearances before award; the company does not share bid success ratio.

qa_highlights.question: Will the doubling of order book be in hydro, and are there very large projects that can move it?
qa_highlights.answer: COO said the order book would be a blend of hydro and transport, largely hydro-led. Chairman-level comment (Dhawan) said large project details cannot be shared, bids are diversified across core segments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt repayment liability due in March, and is the company targeting debt-free status?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about ₹350 crore falls due in March after the Q2 prepayment; Dhawan said the company is on target to be debt-free within the next couple of years.

capex_capacity: Indore Metro: both TBMs running; about 12 km of TBM tunnelling across seven underground stations, one of the largest underground packages in the country.
Bhivpuri PSP (1,000 MW, Tata Power): powerhouse and main access tunnel described as complete; other sections progressing.
Vishnugad Pipalkoti: about 80% complete, 830 m of HRT TBM tunnelling balance, dam about 80% complete.
FRFCF facility about 87% complete; Parwan Dam completed with reservoir filling test done, ancillary works over next three to four months.
Patna Metro: diaphragm wall equipment mobilisation and machine procurement in progress; Agardanda Creek Bridge superstructure erection to start in about a month.
demand_pricing: Order book ₹12,901 crore, led by transportation, followed by hydropower, nuclear and water; Maharashtra largest state exposure, followed by Bihar.
Orders secured in H1 FY27 of ₹524 crore; lowest bidder on bids worth ₹2,010 crore (HCC share ₹1,557 crore).
More than 16 bids worth about ₹34,805 crore under evaluation; strong pipeline of about ₹86,000 crore across sectors.
Management attributed order delays mainly to hydropower tenders awaiting client clearances; more bids submitted in hydro recently.
Management said it will price risk responsibly and remain selective on clients amid commodity price volatility and higher competitive intensity in some segments.
Overseas opportunities: qualified as bidder on some projects, but awards about 12 months away.
risks_watch: Order book conversion: the doubling to about ₹25,000 crore by year-end depends on award of bids worth ₹34,805 crore, with hydro awards dependent on client clearances; analyst questioned whether doubling is a close or distant possibility and COO answered it is a possibility.
Margin trajectory: standalone EBITDA margin fell to 12.2% from 16.1%; management says quarterly margins will not match the 13-14% long-term range.
Consolidated profit drag from interest accruals on loans to insignificant subsidiaries, expected to stop within a couple of quarters.
Debt: about ₹350 crore due in March 2027; ₹108 crore prepayment targeted by December 2026; Supreme Court award money expected in Q3 FY27.
Revenue inconsistency: standalone turnover given as ₹895.8 crore in the presentation and ₹923 crore by the CFO; not reconciled on the call.

BKC bullet train station work progressing slightly behind target; analyst asked for it to be added to presentation. Promoter pledge levels were raised by an investor (82% pledged per question, not addressed by management beyond general intent to increase stake).
key_quotes: So, see this construction business is kind of seasonal business and sometimes you will see that there are some elements of the project with high margins will be executed, sometimes some lower margin projects are executed.
Bid success ratio is a very difficult number to be put out like this, because we are still working on that and largely we don't share this information.
What I will tell you that HCC continues to be very selective with regard to the clients we pick and the contracts we choose.
Our clear imperative is to ensure that we're debt-free as early as possible, which should certainly be, I mean, we're certainly on target to do that next couple of years.

Bhivpuri PSP 1,000 MW powerhouse and main access tunnel complete (client Tata Power asset; HCC contractor work, not own capacity)

growth.why: Management targets the order book doubling from ₹12,901 crore by year-end, backed by ₹2,010 crore of L1 bids (HCC share ₹1,557 crore) and ₹34,805 crore under evaluation, but H1 order inflow was only ₹524 crore and no specific award timing is given; long-term standalone EBITDA margin guided at 13-14%, with Q2 standalone margin at 12.2%, and no capacity additions of the company itself are discussed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin fell to 12.2% from 16.1% YoY, and management guides a 13-14% long-term average but says quarterly margins will not match that range every quarter.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Company's own capacity additions were not discussed; projects listed (Indore Metro, Bhivpuri PSP, Vishnugad, FRFCF) are contractor execution work, not HCC-owned capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of ₹12,901 crore is targeted to roughly double by year-end, but H1 FY27 orders were only ₹524 crore and standalone turnover fell to ₹895.8-923 crore from ₹975 crore YoY, with no award timing given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation were not discussed on the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management was cautious on near-term margins and only held its long-term 13-14% range, with no raised guidance; the order-doubling target is conditional on pending awards.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Order inflow of ₹524 crore in H1 against a target to double the ₹12,901 crore book, and hydro awards delayed by client clearances, leave the year-end target exposed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products or service lines were discussed; this is a contractor, so launches do not apply.

rows.label: Order book doubling to about ₹25,000 crore by year-end
rows.why: Targeted doubling from ₹12,901 crore depends on ₹34,805 crore of bids under evaluation and ₹2,010 crore of L1 positions (HCC share ₹1,557 crore), with COO calling it a possibility rather than a firm plan.

rows.label: Debt prepayment and debt-free target
rows.why: ₹100 crore prepaid in Q2 with a further ₹108 crore targeted by December 2026, leaving about ₹350 crore due in March 2027; management is on target to be debt-free within two years.

rows.label: Supreme Court award money release
rows.why: Management expects award money from a Supreme Court matter to be released in Q3 FY27, which could cut debt or lift cash flow, though the amount was not given.

tone.note: Management was confident on operations and order-book recovery but cautious on near-term margins (12.2% vs 16.1%) and evasive on the bid pipeline, bid success ratio and large project sizes; analysts pressed on the margin fall, consolidated profit drag and whether the order-book doubling is realistic
